text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkish Cypriot involvement in European Union accession talks is put on the back burner until progress is achieved on the Cyprus problem.
- The government puts 13 million ($26.7 million) pounds into farmers' pockets in compensation for the drought.
- There is a "historic opportunity" for direct talks in Cyprus, says the European Union.
- U.N. special envoy Gustave Feissel confirms there has been movement on the indirect military dialogue between the two sides.
- "Forget about (EU) accession before a solution", EU External Affairs Commissioner Hans Van Den Broek tells the political leadership in Cyprus.
- The CIA is determined to stop the deployment of the S-300 Russian missile system in Cyprus, according to a Russian news agency.
- EU official tells Cyprus its accession to Europe may not be endorsed by parliaments of member-states if the Cyprus problem is not solved first.
- Europe is blackmailing Cyprus over accession. The Cyprus problem has to be solved first and then we can become members. ($=0.506 pounds)
